statement: A 64-year-old patient presents with the sudden appearance of multiple, gray-black velvety hyperkeratotic patches in the axillae and groin, alongside several seborrheic keratoses. This clinical combination is most frequently a marker for which underlying malignancy?
options: Hepatocellular carcinoma
Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung
Renal cell adenocarcinoma
Multiple myeloma
Carcinoma of the stomach
correctOption: Carcinoma of the stomach
optionExplanations: Hepatocellular carcinoma is associated with erythrocytosis or hypoglycemia but not primarily with these specific dermatological paraneoplastic syndromes.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung is more classically associated with PTHRP-induced hypercalcemia and hypertrophic osteoarthropathy rather than acanthosis nigricans.
Renal cell carcinoma is often associated with polycythemia or hypercalcemia but is not the primary association for the Leser-Trélat sign.
Multiple myeloma typically presents with hypercalcemia or renal failure but not with velvety skin thickening or eruptive seborrheic keratoses.
Acanthosis nigricans and the Leser-Trélat sign (abrupt seborrheic keratoses) are classic cutaneous markers for internal malignancies, with gastric carcinoma being the most common.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): In about 50% of the cases, particularly in adults older than age 40, the appearance of such lesions [Acanthosis nigricans] is associated with cancer, most commonly carcinoma of the stomach. Acanthosis nigricans is sometimes accompanied by the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses (Leser-Trélat sign).

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 68-year-old male presents with painful, swollen wrists and fingers. Physical examination reveals periosteal new bone formation at the distal ends of the radius and ulna, along with distinct clubbing of the digits. Chest imaging confirms a primary pulmonary malignancy. What is the correct clinical designation for this constellation of findings?
options: Cushing syndrome
Trousseau syndrome
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
correctOption: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
optionExplanations: Cushing syndrome is an endocrinopathy resulting from ectopic ACTH secretion, presenting with hypertension, weight gain, and metabolic changes.
Trousseau syndrome involves migratory thrombophlebitis, which is a vascular paraneoplastic syndrome unrelated to bone formation or finger clubbing.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is defined by the triad of periosteal bone formation, arthritis, and digital clubbing, most often seen in lung cancer patients.
Lambert-Eaton is a neuromuscular syndrome causing muscle weakness, not periosteal bone changes or joint swelling.
NBTE involves small fibrinous vegetations on heart valves and is a vascular paraneoplastic manifestation.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): This disorder is characterized by (1) periosteal new bone formation, primarily at the distal ends of long bones... (2) arthritis of the adjacent joints; and (3) clubbing of the digits. [Referencing Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy]

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 70-year-old female with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinoma of the pancreas develops sudden left-sided weakness and a new heart murmur. Echocardiography reveals small, bland, fibrinous vegetations on the mitral valve leaflets. Which of the following conditions best explains these cardiac findings?
options: Trousseau syndrome
Rheumatic heart disease
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE)
Acute bacterial endocarditis
Libman-Sacks endocarditis
correctOption: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE)
optionExplanations: While related as a vascular manifestation of cancer, Trousseau syndrome specifically refers to migratory thrombophlebitis, not valvular vegetations.
Rheumatic heart disease involves chronic valvular scarring and follows a streptococcal infection, not an acute manifestation of advanced adenocarcinoma.
NBTE is a paraneoplastic vascular manifestation characterized by sterile, bland fibrinous vegetations on valves, frequently associated with advanced mucin-secreting tumors.
Bacterial endocarditis usually presents with fever and large, friable vegetations containing organisms, unlike the bland, sterile vegetations of NBTE.
Libman-Sacks endocarditis is specifically associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) rather than paraneoplastic syndromes in adenocarcinoma.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Bland, small, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations sometimes form on the cardiac valve leaflets... particularly in individuals with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas. These lesions, called nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis...

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Regarding the vascular paraneoplastic manifestations of malignancy, migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) is most strongly associated with which of the following primary tumor sites?
options: Benign meningioma
Medullary carcinoma of the thyroid
Squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus
Basal cell carcinoma of the skin
Carcinoma of the pancreas
correctOption: Carcinoma of the pancreas
optionExplanations: Meningiomas are typically benign and localized, lacking the systemic paraneoplastic vascular effects associated with aggressive adenocarcinomas.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma is associated with calcitonin secretion but not with migratory thrombophlebitis.
Esophageal carcinoma is not the classic association for Trousseau syndrome; it more often presents with local invasion or obstructive symptoms.
Basal cell carcinoma is a localized skin cancer that almost never metastasizes or causes systemic paraneoplastic syndromes like migratory thrombophlebitis.
Pancreatic carcinoma is the classic and most frequent association with migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) due to the release of procoagulants.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) may be encountered in association with deep-seated cancers, most often carcinomas of the pancreas or lung.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A patient with suspected lung cancer presents with moon facies, truncal obesity, and hypertension. Laboratory analysis shows significantly elevated serum ACTH levels that are not suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone. Which paraneoplastic syndrome is this patient exhibiting?
options: Cushing syndrome
Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH)
Carcinoid syndrome
Hypercalcemia
Hypoglycemia
correctOption: Cushing syndrome
optionExplanations: Ectopic secretion of corticotropin (ACTH) by tumors, most notably small cell lung carcinoma, leads to paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome with classic features like moon facies and hypertension.
SIADH involves water retention and hyponatremia due to inappropriate ADH secretion, not the glucocorticoid effects of ACTH.
Carcinoid syndrome involves flushing and diarrhea due to serotonin, not the ACTH-mediated features described.
Hypercalcemia involves calcium metabolism (PTHRP), not the glucocorticoid/ACTH pathway seen here.
Paraneoplastic hypoglycemia is usually associated with insulin-like factors, not ACTH.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 272 (Book Page): For example, bronchogenic carcinomas may produce corticotropin... giving rise to paraneoplastic syndromes.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which of the following paraneoplastic manifestations is correctly paired with the tumor most frequently associated with its clinical development?
options: Trousseau syndrome — Osteosarcoma
Acanthosis nigricans — Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
Hypercalcemia — Basal cell carcinoma
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy — Lung carcinoma
Cushing syndrome — Prostatic adenocarcinoma
correctOption: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy — Lung carcinoma
optionExplanations: Trousseau syndrome is associated with pancreas or lung carcinomas, not bone-forming sarcomas.
Acanthosis nigricans is primarily associated with visceral cancers, specifically gastric carcinoma, rather than common skin cancers.
Hypercalcemia is common in squamous cell lung cancer, breast, and renal cancer, but not in basal cell carcinoma, which rarely has systemic effects.
Lung carcinoma is the preeminent cause of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy, occurring in up to 10% of cases.
Cushing syndrome is most commonly associated with small cell carcinoma of the lung, while prostate cancer is more associated with DIC.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is encountered in 1% to 10% of patients with lung carcinoma.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 45-year-old male with a history of bruising and bleeding is diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). He suddenly develops widespread petechiae and laboratory evidence of fibrinogen depletion and prolonged clotting times. Which paraneoplastic hematologic manifestation is most likely?
options: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
Erythrocytosis
Polycythemia vera
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
Migratory thrombophlebitis
correctOption: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
optionExplanations: DIC is a severe paraneoplastic complication characterized by systemic activation of coagulation and consumption of factors, classically associated with APL.
Erythrocytosis (excess red cells) is a paraneoplastic effect of EPO secretion, not a bleeding disorder.
Polycythemia vera is a primary myeloproliferative neoplasm, not a paraneoplastic manifestation of leukemia.
NBTE involves valvular vegetations which may embolize, but doesn't typically present as a systemic bleeding disorder like APL-related DIC.
Migratory thrombophlebitis involves focal, moving venous clots, not the systemic consumptive coagulopathy seen in DIC.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Disseminated intravascular coagulation may complicate a diversity of clinical disorders... among cancers, it is most commonly associated with acute promyelocytic leukemia and prostatic adenocarcinoma.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Paraneoplastic syndromes are clinically significant for which of the following reasons?
options: They may represent the earliest manifestation of an occult neoplasm.
They are easily treated by simple surgical resection of the symptoms.
They always signify that the tumor has already metastasized to distant organs.
They result from the release of hormones indigenous to the tumor's cell of origin.
They are caused by the direct mechanical compression of nerves by the primary tumor.
correctOption: They may represent the earliest manifestation of an occult neoplasm.
optionExplanations: Syndromes like Acanthosis nigricans or hypercalcemia can be the very first sign of a cancer that has not yet been detected (occult).
Treatment requires addressing the underlying malignancy, as simple symptomatic treatment of the paraneoplastic effect is usually insufficient or temporary.
Paraneoplastic syndromes do not necessarily mean metastasis; they can occur with small, localized, or even occult primary tumors.
Paraneoplastic syndromes are specifically defined as effects NOT explained by the release of hormones indigenous to the tissue of origin.
By definition, paraneoplastic syndromes are not caused by direct mechanical effects or compression by the tumor.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): These skin changes [Acanthosis nigricans] may appear before the cancer is discovered. [Context: Clinical features of syndromes].

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which of the following clinical conditions is specifically referred to as Trousseau syndrome when it manifests as a paraneoplastic phenomenon associated with visceral malignancies?
options: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
Acanthosis nigricans
Migratory thrombophlebitis
correctOption: Migratory thrombophlebitis
optionExplanations: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) is a complex coagulopathy often associated with acute promyelocytic leukemia or prostate cancer, but the eponym Trousseau refers specifically to the migratory venous inflammation.

Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) involves sterile vegetations on heart valves, typically in advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas, but is not termed Trousseau syndrome. It is a separate vascular/hematologic manifestation.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is a skeletal paraneoplastic syndrome involving clubbing and periosteal bone formation, unrelated to the thrombotic events of Trousseau syndrome.
Acanthosis nigricans is a dermatological paraneoplastic syndrome characterized by hyperpigmented, velvety skin patches, often associated with gastric carcinoma, not vascular inflammation.

Trousseau syndrome is the classic eponym for migratory thrombophlebitis, where multiple sites of venous inflammation appear and resolve in succession, signaling an underlying malignancy like pancreatic or lung cancer.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) may be encountered in association with deep-seated cancers, most often carcinomas of the pancreas or lung.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: In the context of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia, which mechanism best explains the elevation of serum calcium in a patient with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung who lacks evidence of skeletal metastasis?
options: Release of interleukin-1 (IL-1) and TNF by osteolytic lesions
Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to chronic renal failure
Synthesis of calcitonin by the neoplastic epithelial cells
Ectopic secretion of native parathyroid hormone (PTH)
Production of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHRP)
correctOption: Production of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHRP)
optionExplanations: IL-1 and TNF are factors that can contribute to hypercalcemia through osteolysis, but the text notes that in squamous cell carcinoma specifically, the primary mechanism is the humoral release of PTHRP.
Secondary hyperparathyroidism is a physiological response to hypocalcemia (often due to renal failure) and is not a paraneoplastic syndrome initiated by a tumor cell's ectopic secretion of factors.
Calcitonin is a hormone that lowers serum calcium and is used as a marker for medullary carcinoma of the thyroid; its synthesis would not explain hypercalcemia.
While paraneoplastic syndromes involve hormone-like substances, tumors rarely produce the actual native PTH molecule; instead, they produce an analog that acts on the same receptors.

Squamous cell carcinomas of the lung frequently produce PTHRP (parathyroid hormone-related protein). This protein mimics the action of PTH on bone and kidney, leading to hypercalcemia even in the absence of direct bony invasion.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The most common lung neoplasm associated with hypercalcemia is squamous cell carcinoma, typically because of release of PTHRP.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which of the following clinical triads is diagnostic for hypertrophic osteoarthropathy in a patient diagnosed with lung carcinoma?
options: Cushingoid facies, hypercalcemia, and clubbing of digits
Periosteal new bone formation, arthritis, and clubbing of digits
Neuromuscular weakness, sensory loss, and periosteal thinning
Migratory thrombophlebitis, clubbing, and arthritis
Clubbing of digits, dermatitis, and hyperkeratosis
correctOption: Periosteal new bone formation, arthritis, and clubbing of digits
optionExplanations: Cushingoid facies and hypercalcemia are endocrinopathies (Cushing and PTHRP secretion) and do not belong to the skeletal syndrome of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.

The classic paraneoplastic presentation in lung cancer (1%–10% of cases) involves the combination of digital clubbing, inflammation of the joints (arthritis), and the radiographic finding of periosteal new bone at the distal ends of long bones.
While neuromyopathic syndromes can involve weakness, hypertrophic osteoarthropathy involves specific skeletal findings like periosteal thickening, not thinning or sensory loss.
Migratory thrombophlebitis is part of Trousseau syndrome; while both can occur in lung cancer, they represent distinct paraneoplastic entities.
Dermatitis and hyperkeratosis are features of skin disorders like acanthosis nigricans, not the skeletal changes seen in hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): This disorder is characterized by (1) periosteal new bone formation, primarily at the distal ends of long bones... (2) arthritis of the adjacent joints; and (3) clubbing of the digits .

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 65-year-old heavy smoker presents with progressive gait instability and loss of fine motor coordination. Imaging reveals a 4 cm mass in the right upper lobe. No brain metastases are found on MRI. What is the most likely pathophysiological basis for his neurological symptoms according to the established patterns of paraneoplastic syndromes?
options: Ischemic necrosis of the motor cortex due to nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
A cancer-induced immunologic attack on the cerebellum using cross-reacting antibodies
Direct compression of the spinal cord by the primary lung tumor
Electrolyte imbalances resulting from the secretion of atrial natriuretic peptide
Metabolic derangements caused by tumor-induced Cushing syndrome
correctOption: A cancer-induced immunologic attack on the cerebellum using cross-reacting antibodies
optionExplanations: While NBTE can cause emboli and strokes, the chronic, progressive presentation of gait instability described is more characteristic of the neurodegenerative paraneoplastic syndromes mentioned in the text.

The text explains that neuromyopathic syndromes like cortical cerebellar degeneration result from an immune-mediated mechanism where the body produces T-cells or antibodies against tumor antigens that inadvertently target normal neuronal tissues.
Direct compression would be a local effect of the tumor mass or spread, whereas a paraneoplastic syndrome is defined as a symptom complex that cannot be explained by direct tumor spread.

Electrolyte imbalances can cause confusion or seizures, but the specific presentation of cerebellar dysfunction is attributed to the immunologic neuropathic syndromes in the context of neoplasia research cited in the text.

Cushing syndrome primarily causes metabolic effects like weight gain and hypertension, and while it may cause proximal muscle weakness, it does not typically present as cortical cerebellar degeneration (ataxia).
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The cause of these syndromes is poorly understood, but appears to involve a cancer-induced immunologic attack on normal tissues... In some cases, antibodies that cross-react with neuronal cell antigens are detected.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which specific histological category of malignancy is most characteristically associated with the formation of bland, sterile fibrinous vegetations on heart valves as part of a paraneoplastic syndrome?
options: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
Hepatocellular carcinoma
Mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas
Small cell carcinoma of the lung
correctOption: Mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas
optionExplanations: While leukemias can be associated with DIC (especially promyelocytic), NBTE is specifically highlighted as a feature of advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas of the viscera like the colon or pancreas.
Squamous cell carcinomas are more frequently linked to PTHRP-mediated hypercalcemia rather than the hypercoagulable states that lead to sterile heart valve vegetations.
Hepatocellular carcinoma is mentioned in the text as being associated with Alpha-fetoprotein, but it is not the primary association listed for NBTE.

The text explicitly links the development of NBTE vegetations with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas. The mucin is thought to play a role in activating the coagulation cascade in these patients.
Small cell carcinoma is most famous for endocrinopathies like Cushing syndrome (ACTH production), but not specifically NBTE.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Bland, small, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations sometimes form on the cardiac valve leaflets... particularly in individuals with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: The 'Leser-Trélat sign' is a dermatological manifestation characterized by the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses. According to clinical pathology, this sign is frequently associated with which of the following?
options: Renal cell adenocarcinoma
Acanthosis nigricans and stomach carcinoma
Bronchogenic squamous cell carcinoma
Hypercalcemia and medullary thyroid carcinoma
Trousseau syndrome and pancreatic cancer
correctOption: Acanthosis nigricans and stomach carcinoma
optionExplanations: Renal cell carcinoma is often linked to polycythemia (via erythropoietin) or hypercalcemia, but not the Leser-Trélat sign.

The text clarifies that Acanthosis nigricans (velvety skin patches) is often seen with the Leser-Trélat sign (multiple seborrheic keratoses) in the context of visceral cancers, most classically stomach carcinoma.
Bronchogenic carcinoma is more commonly linked to Cushing syndrome or hypercalcemia; seborrheic keratoses are not its hallmark paraneoplastic skin finding.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma produces calcitonin and is not associated with the seborrheic keratosis eruptions of the Leser-Trélat sign.
Trousseau syndrome is a vascular phenomenon; while it can occur alongside skin signs, it is not the definition of or the primary association for the Leser-Trélat sign.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Acanthosis nigricans is sometimes accompanied by the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses (Leser-Trélat sign)... associated with cancer, most commonly carcinoma of the stomach.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A patient with breast cancer develops significant hypercalcemia. Evaluation reveals no skeletal metastases on a bone scan. Which factor, besides PTHRP, is cited as a possible humoral cause for this paraneoplastic endocrinopathy?
options: Transforming growth factor-alpha (TGF-α)
Corticotropin (ACTH)
Insulin-like growth factor (IGF-1)
Antidiuretic hormone (ADH)
Erythropoietin
correctOption: Transforming growth factor-alpha (TGF-α)
optionExplanations: The text lists TGF-α as one of the factors (along with IL-1, TNF, and Vitamin D analogs) that can be produced by tumors to induce hypercalcemia humorally.
Corticotropin (ACTH) is the cause of paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome, not hypercalcemia.
IGF-1 is a mitogen involved in normal growth and some tumor growth signaling, but it is not listed as a mediator of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia in the text.
Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) secretion leads to the Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH (SIADH), which causes hyponatremia, not hypercalcemia.
Erythropoietin is associated with polycythemia, a paraneoplastic increase in red blood cell mass, not calcium regulation.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): In addition to PTHRP, several other factors, such as IL-1, TGF- α , TNF, and dihydroxyvitamin D, have been causally implicated in the hypercalcemia of malignancy.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 58-year-old male with a history of weight loss and epigastric pain presents with a painful, erythematous, linear cord-like swelling on his left forearm. Three days later, the swelling resolves but a similar lesion appears on his right thigh. Which underlying malignancy is most strongly suspected based on this paraneoplastic feature?
options: Small cell carcinoma of the lung
Osteosarcoma of the femur
Carcinoma of the pancreas
Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
Medullary carcinoma of the thyroid
correctOption: Carcinoma of the pancreas
optionExplanations: While lung cancer can cause this, pancreatic cancer is the classic visceral malignancy associated with the epigastric pain and Trousseau syndrome combination described.
Osteosarcoma is a primary bone tumor that does not typically present with migratory venous inflammation.

The patient is presenting with migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome), which is characterized by venous inflammation that changes locations. The text specifically highlights pancreas and lung carcinomas as the most common deep-seated cancers associated with this finding.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin is a localized malignancy that does not typically cause systemic paraneoplastic vascular syndromes like migratory thrombophlebitis.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma is associated with calcitonin production and MEN syndromes, not migratory thrombophlebitis.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) may be encountered in association with deep-seated cancers, most often carcinomas of the pancreas or lung.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Certain bronchogenic carcinomas produce a substance that mimics the clinical features of Cushing syndrome. What is the metabolic or physiological consequence of this ectopic production?
options: Hypoglycemia due to insulin-like activity
Polycythemia due to erythropoietin-like activity
Hypocalcemia due to excessive calcitonin
Hypercortisolism due to ACTH-like activity
Hyponatremia due to inappropriate ADH secretion
correctOption: Hypercortisolism due to ACTH-like activity
optionExplanations: While some tumors can produce insulin-like substances leading to hypoglycemia, Cushing syndrome is defined by the opposite—hyperglycemic and catabolic effects of excess cortisol.
Polycythemia is caused by erythropoietin, often seen in renal or hepatic tumors, not as part of Cushing syndrome.
Calcitonin production would lead to hypocalcemia, which is not the mechanism of Cushing syndrome.

Cushing syndrome in the paraneoplastic context is caused by the ectopic production of corticotropin (ACTH) or ACTH-like substances by tumors (like bronchogenic carcinoma), leading to excessive cortisol production by the adrenal glands.
Hyponatremia is the result of SIADH (antidiuretic hormone), a different paraneoplastic syndrome also seen in lung cancers but distinct from Cushing.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 272 (Book Page): For example, bronchogenic carcinomas may produce corticotropin, parathyroid-like hormone, insulin, glucagon, and other hormones, giving rise to paraneoplastic syndromes.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which paraneoplastic skin disorder is described as gray-black patches of thickened, velvety skin, often appearing as a harbinger of an underlying gastric malignancy?
options: Pemphigus vulgaris
Seborrheic keratosis
Acanthosis nigricans
Dermatomyositis
Migratory thrombophlebitis
correctOption: Acanthosis nigricans
optionExplanations: Pemphigus vulgaris is an autoimmune blistering disease, not a common paraneoplastic velvety skin condition mentioned in this context.
Seborrheic keratoses are the 'Leser-Trélat sign' components, but they are warty lesions, not diffuse velvety patches.
Acanthosis nigricans is the classic description for velvety, hyperpigmented skin patches in flexural areas that often signal an internal malignancy, particularly in the stomach.
Dermatomyositis is an inflammatory muscle and skin disease; while it can be paraneoplastic, it does not match the description of velvety gray-black patches.
Migratory thrombophlebitis is a vascular condition involving painful veins, not a skin-surface texture disorder.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Acanthosis nigricans is a disorder characterized by gray-black patches of thickened, hyperkeratotic skin with a velvety appearance... associated with cancer, most commonly carcinoma of the stomach.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
coreConcept: Acanthosis Nigricans as a Paraneoplastic Skin Disorder
statement: A 52-year-old male is diagnosed with stomach carcinoma. Physical examination reveals gray-black patches of thickened, hyperkeratotic skin with a velvety texture in the axilla and neck regions. Which of the following paraneoplastic conditions is most likely represented by these findings?
options: Trousseau syndrome
Acanthosis nigricans
Leser-Trélat sign
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
Dermatomyositis
correctOption: Acanthosis nigricans
optionExplanations: Trousseau syndrome, or migratory thrombophlebitis, is a vascular paraneoplastic syndrome involving venous inflammation and clots, not skin texture changes.
Acanthosis nigricans is a paraneoplastic manifestation presenting as velvety, hyperpigmented skin patches, often associated with abdominal malignancies like gastric carcinoma.
The Leser-Trélat sign refers specifically to the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses, not simply the velvety hyperpigmented patches described.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy involves periosteal new bone formation and clubbing, typically associated with lung carcinoma, not hyperpigmented skin patches.
Dermatomyositis is an inflammatory myopathy with characteristic rashes (heliotrope/Gottron papules) not velvety hyperpigmentation.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Acanthosis nigricans is a disorder characterized by gray-black patches of thickened, hyperkeratotic skin with a velvety appearance... associated with cancer, most commonly carcinoma of the stomach.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: In the context of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia, which of the following best describes the most common pathophysiological mechanism associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung?
options: Secretion of insulin-like growth factors by the primary tumor
Direct osteolytic destruction of bone by metastatic deposits
Release of excessive Vitamin D by tumor-associated macrophages
Ectopic production of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHRP)
Production of Interleukin-1 (IL-1) leading to generalized bone resorption
correctOption: Ectopic production of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHRP)
optionExplanations: Insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) are associated with tumor growth and metabolic effects but do not classically mediate paraneoplastic hypercalcemia.
While osteolytic metastases can cause hypercalcemia (especially in breast cancer), the paraneoplastic form in squamous cell lung cancer is typically biochemical and systemic.
While dihydroxyvitamin D can be involved in some malignancies, PTHRP is the classic and most common mediator in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
PTHRP is the primary mediator of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia, mimicking the action of parathyroid hormone but being tumor-derived and biochemically distinct.
IL-1 and other cytokines (TNF, TGF-alpha) are implicated in the hypercalcemia of malignancy but are less common specific drivers than PTHRP in this histological type.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The most common lung neoplasm associated with hypercalcemia is squamous cell carcinoma, typically because of release of PTHRP.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A patient with a lung malignancy is evaluated for a suspected skeletal paraneoplastic syndrome. Which triad of clinical features would most accurately support a diagnosis of Hypertrophic Osteoarthropathy (HOA)?
options: Verrucous skin lesions, arthritis, and periosteal thickening
Digital clubbing, seborrheic keratosis, and osteolytic lesions
Pathological fractures, hypercalcemia, and bone pain
Periosteal new bone formation, arthritis, and digital clubbing
Osteoblastic lesions, hypocalcemia, and joint stiffness
correctOption: Periosteal new bone formation, arthritis, and digital clubbing
optionExplanations: Verrucous lesions (seborrheic keratoses) are part of the Leser-Trélat sign, not HOA.
While digital clubbing is a feature of HOA, seborrheic keratosis and osteolytic lesions are associated with other paraneoplastic or metastatic processes.
These features suggest bone metastases and hypercalcemia rather than the specific paraneoplastic syndrome of HOA.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is defined by the combination of digital clubbing, periosteal new bone at distal long bones, and arthritis.
HOA involves new bone formation (periosteal) but not specifically osteoblastic lesions (which are typically metastatic) and is not characterized by hypocalcemia.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): This disorder is characterized by (1) periosteal new bone formation, primarily at the distal ends of long bones... (2) arthritis of the adjacent joints; and (3) clubbing of the digits.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 68-year-old male with known pancreatic adenocarcinoma presents with sudden onset of migratory warmth, redness, and tenderness in his left calf, followed two days later by similar symptoms in his right thigh. Physical examination reveals cord-like subcutaneous structures in the affected areas. What is the most likely paraneoplastic mechanism at work?
options: Secretion of procoagulant factors by the tumor cells
Immune complex deposition in small cutaneous vessels
Direct invasion of the venous plexus by tumor cells
Ectopic production of erythropoietin
Autoimmune attack on vascular endothelial cells
correctOption: Secretion of procoagulant factors by the tumor cells
optionExplanations: Pancreatic cancers often release procoagulants or mucins that trigger the coagulation cascade, leading to the migratory thrombophlebitis known as Trousseau syndrome.
Immune complex deposition characterizes vasculitides like Henoch-Schonlein Purpura, not paraneoplastic Trousseau syndrome.
Migratory thrombophlebitis occurs at sites distant from the primary tumor and is not caused by direct invasion.
Ectopic erythropoietin production causes polycythemia (elevated RBCs), which can increase viscosity but is not the specific mechanism for migratory thrombophlebitis.
Trousseau syndrome is not primarily an autoimmune vasculitis but a hypercoagulable state.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): As mentioned in the discussion of thrombosis (Chapter 4), migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) may be encountered in association with deep-seated cancers, most often carcinomas of the pancreas or lung.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: The neuromyopathic paraneoplastic syndromes, such as cerebellar degeneration and myasthenic syndromes, are currently believed to be caused by which of the following biological processes?
options: Ischemic damage from tumor-induced hyperviscosity
Direct viral infection of neurons due to immunosuppression
Immunologic cross-reactivity between tumor antigens and neuronal tissues
Metabolic toxins released during tumor necrosis
Competitive inhibition of neurotransmitter receptors by ectopic hormones
correctOption: Immunologic cross-reactivity between tumor antigens and neuronal tissues
optionExplanations: Hyperviscosity typically presents with headache, vision changes, and global deficits rather than targeted degeneration like cerebellar syndromes.
While immunosuppression can lead to viral infections (like PML), neuromyopathic paraneoplastic syndromes are specifically defined as immune-mediated reactions to the cancer itself.
The ectopic expression of specific antigens by tumor cells triggers an immune response (T-cells or antibodies) that cross-reacts with similar antigens in the nervous system.
Necrotic toxins generally cause systemic inflammatory responses (like fever) rather than specific neurological degeneration.
These syndromes involve tissue damage and degeneration rather than simple receptor blockade by hormones like PTHRP or ACTH.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The cause of these syndromes is poorly understood, but appears to involve a cancer-induced immunologic attack on normal tissues. The initiating event may be the ectopic expression of antigens that normally are restricted to the neuromuscular system by tumor cells.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: By definition, which of the following criteria must be met for a clinical symptom complex to be classified as a paraneoplastic syndrome?
options: It must result from the release of hormones indigenous to the tumor's tissue of origin.
It cannot be explained by the local or distant spread of the tumor.
It must be caused by direct metastatic spread of the tumor cells.
It must involve only the endocrine system or metabolic pathways.
It must occur only in advanced, terminal stages of the malignancy.
correctOption: It cannot be explained by the local or distant spread of the tumor.
optionExplanations: If a thyroid tumor produces thyroid hormone, it is a functional tumor, not a paraneoplastic syndrome; paraneoplastic hormones must be 'ectopic' or non-indigenous.
The hallmark of a paraneoplastic syndrome is that its manifestations are remote from the tumor and its metastases and not explained by normal cell-of-origin products.
If a symptom is caused by metastasis (e.g., bone pain from a secondary deposit), it is not paraneoplastic.
Paraneoplastic syndromes can be vascular, neurologic, dermatologic, or skeletal, not just endocrine.
These syndromes can be the earliest sign of an occult malignancy and do not necessarily require advanced disease stages.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Paraneoplastic syndromes: symptom complexes in individuals with cancer that cannot be explained by tumor spread or release of hormones that are indigenous to the tumor 'cell of origin.'

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: The abrupt development of numerous seborrheic keratoses, often occurring in conjunction with acanthosis nigricans in a patient with an occult internal malignancy, is known as which of the following?
options: Lambert-Eaton syndrome
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
Cushing syndrome
Leser-Trélat sign
Trousseau sign
correctOption: Leser-Trélat sign
optionExplanations: Lambert-Eaton is a myasthenic syndrome involving muscle weakness, not dermatological findings.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy involves bone and joints, specifically periosteal changes and clubbing.
Cushing syndrome refers to hypercortisolism, which may present with striae and buffalo hump, but not seborrheic keratoses.
The Leser-Trélat sign is the clinical hallmark for the sudden eruption of seborrheic keratoses associated with internal malignancy.
The Trousseau sign refers to migratory thrombophlebitis or clinical tetany, not skin lesions.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Acanthosis nigricans is sometimes accompanied by the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses (Leser-Trélat sign).

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
coreConcept: Ectopic ACTH and Paraneoplastic Cushing Syndrome
statement: A 55-year-old heavy smoker presents with a central hilar lung mass, hypertension, weight gain, and muscle weakness. Laboratory studies reveal hypokalemia and elevated serum corticotropin (ACTH) levels. What is the most likely paraneoplastic mechanism contributing to his clinical presentation?
options: Autoimmune destruction of the adrenal cortex
Production of tumor necrosis factor leading to cachexia
Ectopic production of ACTH by the bronchogenic carcinoma
Ectopic secretion of Parathyroid Hormone-Related Protein
Primary hyperaldosteronism due to an adrenal adenoma
correctOption: Ectopic production of ACTH by the bronchogenic carcinoma
optionExplanations: Adrenal destruction (Addison's) would cause hypotension, hyperkalemia, and weight loss, the opposite of the presentation.
TNF (cachectin) leads to profound weight loss and muscle wasting (cachexia), whereas this patient has weight gain and Cushingoid features.
Bronchogenic carcinomas (particularly small cell type) are known to ectopically secrete ACTH (corticotropin), leading to paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome.
PTHRP causes hypercalcemia, not the hypertension, hypokalemia, and Cushingoid features seen with ACTH.
While primary hyperaldosteronism causes hypertension and hypokalemia, it does not explain the presence of a lung mass or elevated ACTH.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 272 (Book Page): For example, bronchogenic carcinomas may produce corticotropin, parathyroid-like hormone, insulin, glucagon, and other hormones, giving rise to paraneoplastic syndromes.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Bland, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations found on the cardiac valves of a patient with an advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinoma are characteristic of which paraneoplastic condition?
options: Libman-Sacks endocarditis
Rheumatic heart disease
Infective endocarditis
Marantic myocarditis
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
correctOption: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
optionExplanations: Libman-Sacks endocarditis is associated with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), not paraneoplastic syndromes of cancer.
Rheumatic heart disease involves sterile vegetations but is an inflammatory sequel to streptococcal infection, not a paraneoplastic syndrome.
Infective endocarditis involves microbial colonization of the valves, whereas NBTE vegetations are 'bland' and sterile.
The term is endocarditis (valvular), not myocarditis (muscle), and 'marantic' is an older synonym for NBTE, but the text uses the specific pathologic term NBTE.
NBTE involves small, sterile fibrinous vegetations on valves, often as a paraneoplastic manifestation of advanced cancers.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Bland, small, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations sometimes form on the cardiac valve leaflets... particularly in individuals with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas. These lesions, called nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis...

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which of the following malignancies is most frequently associated with the paraneoplastic manifestation of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)?
options: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin
Prostatic adenocarcinoma
Renal cell carcinoma
Benign follicular thyroid adenoma
Hepatocellular carcinoma
correctOption: Prostatic adenocarcinoma
optionExplanations: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin is rarely associated with systemic paraneoplastic hematologic syndromes.
Prostatic adenocarcinoma and acute promyelocytic leukemia are the two specific malignancies cited as most commonly associated with paraneoplastic DIC.
Renal cell carcinoma is more commonly associated with hypercalcemia or erythrocytosis than DIC.
A benign follicular adenoma is not a malignancy and does not typically trigger paraneoplastic syndromes like DIC.
Hepatocellular carcinoma is not specifically highlighted as a leading paraneoplastic cause of DIC in the text.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Disseminated intravascular coagulation may complicate a diversity of clinical disorders (Chapter 14); among cancers, it is most commonly associated with acute promyelocytic leukemia and prostatic adenocarcinoma.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 58-year-old male is diagnosed with a lung tumor. The clinician notes that the patient has developed significant clinical symptoms that cannot be explained by the local or distant anatomical spread of the tumor, nor by the physiological hormones typically produced by the tissue of origin. Which of the following best defines this clinical phenomenon?
options: Tumor lysis syndrome
Cachexia
Ectopic hormone replacement
Paraneoplastic syndrome
Metastatic sequelae
correctOption: Paraneoplastic syndrome
optionExplanations: Tumor lysis syndrome is a metabolic crisis caused by the rapid breakdown of cancer cells during chemotherapy, leading to hyperkalemia and hyperuricemia, rather than a syndrome of ectopic product release.

Cachexia is the progressive loss of body fat and lean body mass due to systemic inflammation and metabolic changes in cancer, but it is considered a general systemic effect rather than a specific paraneoplastic syndrome like Cushing or hypercalcemia.
Ectopic hormone replacement is not a standard medical term; ectopic hormone production is the mechanism behind some paraneoplastic syndromes, but the term itself describes the clinical complex.

Paraneoplastic syndromes are defined as symptom complexes in cancer patients that are not attributable to the local or metastatic effects of the tumor or hormones typical of the tissue from which the tumor arose.

Metastatic sequelae refer to symptoms directly caused by the physical presence and growth of tumor cells in secondary organs, which is explicitly excluded by the definition of paraneoplastic syndromes.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 331 (Book Page): Paraneoplastic syndromes: symptom complexes in individuals with cancer that cannot be explained by tumor spread or release of hormones that are indigenous to the tumor “cell of origin.”

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: In the context of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia, which of the following describes the most common pathophysiological mechanism associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung?
options: Osteolytic bone destruction by metastatic cells
Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to renal failure
Production of Parathyroid Hormone-Related Protein (PTHRP)
Direct secretion of native Parathyroid Hormone (PTH)
Synthesis of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D by tumor cells
correctOption: Production of Parathyroid Hormone-Related Protein (PTHRP)
optionExplanations: While osteolytic bone metastasis can cause hypercalcemia (common in breast cancer), it is a direct effect of spread, whereas PTHRP production is the classic paraneoplastic mechanism for squamous cell carcinoma.
Secondary hyperparathyroidism is a physiological response to low calcium (often in renal failure) and is not a paraneoplastic syndrome caused by tumor products.

The primary paraneoplastic mechanism for hypercalcemia in many solid tumors, especially squamous cell carcinoma of the lung, is the ectopic secretion of PTHRP, which mimics PTH action on bone and kidneys.
Native PTH secretion by non-endocrine tumors is extremely rare; instead, these tumors produce a peptide (PTHRP) that is related to but distinct from native PTH.
Secretion of dihydroxyvitamin D is a paraneoplastic mechanism more commonly associated with certain lymphomas, not squamous cell carcinomas.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The most common lung neoplasm associated with hypercalcemia is squamous cell carcinoma, typically because of release of PTHRP.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A patient with gastric carcinoma presents with gray-black, velvety, hyperkeratotic patches on the skin. Simultaneously, the patient develops an abrupt onset of multiple seborrheic keratoses. Which of the following terms specifically describes the latter dermatological finding?
options: Acanthosis nigricans
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
Trousseau syndrome
Dermatomyositis
Leser-Trélat sign
correctOption: Leser-Trélat sign
optionExplanations: Acanthosis nigricans refers to the velvety, hyperpigmented patches of skin themselves, not the sudden appearance of seborrheic keratoses.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy involves periosteal bone formation and clubbing, primarily affecting the skeletal system rather than presenting as keratoses.
Trousseau syndrome is migratory thrombophlebitis, a vascular paraneoplastic manifestation involving clotting in different venous sites, unrelated to keratoses.
Dermatomyositis is an inflammatory condition of the muscles and skin that can be paraneoplastic but presents with a heliotrope rash and muscle weakness, not seborrheic keratoses.
The Leser-Trélat sign is defined as the sudden eruption of multiple seborrheic keratoses, which is often a paraneoplastic marker for internal malignancy, particularly gastric adenocarcinoma.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Acanthosis nigricans is sometimes accompanied by the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses (Leser-Trélat sign).

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 64-year-old male with a 40-pack-year smoking history presents with pain in his wrists and ankles. Physical examination reveals clubbing of the fingers and toes. Radiographic imaging demonstrates new periosteal bone formation at the distal ends of the radius and tibia. Which of the following paraneoplastic syndromes and associated primary malignancies is most likely present?
options: Cushing syndrome; Small cell lung carcinoma
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy; Lung carcinoma
Hypercalcemia; Renal cell carcinoma
Migratory thrombophlebitis; Pancreatic carcinoma
Acanthosis nigricans; Gastric carcinoma
correctOption: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy; Lung carcinoma
optionExplanations: Cushing syndrome presents with metabolic features (obesity, hypertension) due to ACTH release; it does not explain the periosteal bone changes or digital clubbing.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is a classic paraneoplastic syndrome associated with lung carcinoma, characterized by the triad of periosteal new bone, arthritis, and digital clubbing.
While hypercalcemia can occur in renal cell carcinoma, it does not present with clubbing or periosteal new bone formation.
Migratory thrombophlebitis presents with tender, erythematous venous cords that resolve and reappear elsewhere; it does not cause bone deposition.
Acanthosis nigricans is a skin disorder (hyperpigmented velvety patches) and does not involve the periosteum or joint changes described in the vignette.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is encountered in 1% to 10% of patients with lung carcinoma... This disorder is characterized by (1) periosteal new bone formation... (2) arthritis... and (3) clubbing of the digits.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Neuromyopathic paraneoplastic syndromes, such as cerebellar degeneration or myasthenic syndromes, are believed to arise from which underlying pathophysiological mechanism?
options: Competitive inhibition of neurotransmitter receptors by ectopic hormones
Immunologic attack on normal tissues due to ectopic expression of neuronal antigens by tumor cells
Ischemic damage to the vasa nervorum due to tumor-induced hypercoagulability
Metabolic neurotoxicity caused by tumor-derived lactic acid
Direct infiltration of the central nervous system by micrometastases
correctOption: Immunologic attack on normal tissues due to ectopic expression of neuronal antigens by tumor cells
optionExplanations: While some syndromes (like Lambert-Eaton) involve receptors, the mechanism is antibody-mediated (immune) rather than hormonal competitive inhibition by ectopic peptides.

The current understanding is that tumor cells ectopically express antigens normally restricted to neurons; the immune system sees these as foreign, producing T-cells and antibodies that cross-react with normal nervous tissue.
Vasa nervorum damage causes neuropathies in diabetes or vasculitis, but the specific neuromyopathic paraneoplastic syndromes described are primarily immunologic/autoimmune.
Lactic acid may cause general fatigue or acidosis, but there is no evidence it specifically targets the cerebellum or neuromuscular junction in a paraneoplastic fashion.
Direct infiltration is a metastatic effect, not a paraneoplastic syndrome, as paraneoplastic effects must occur in the absence of local tumor spread.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The cause of these syndromes... appears to involve a cancer-induced immunologic attack on normal tissues. The initiating event may be the ectopic expression of antigens that normally are restricted to the neuromuscular system by tumor cells.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which of the following clinical findings constitutes the paraneoplastic manifestation known as Trousseau syndrome?
options: Disseminated intravascular coagulation in prostatic cancer
Migratory thrombophlebitis associated with internal malignancy
Nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations on cardiac valves
Peripheral neuropathy with muscle wasting
Velvety gray-black patches in the axilla
correctOption: Migratory thrombophlebitis associated with internal malignancy
optionExplanations: DIC is a hypercoagulable state but is generally described as a systemic consumptive coagulopathy rather than the specific 'migratory thrombophlebitis' defined as Trousseau syndrome.
Trousseau syndrome is the classic term for migratory thrombophlebitis, where patients develop venous clots that appear, resolve, and then reappear in different sites.
Fibrinous vegetations on valves are characteristic of Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis (NBTE), a separate paraneoplastic syndrome from Trousseau syndrome.
Peripheral neuropathy is a neuromyopathic paraneoplastic syndrome, not a vascular/thrombotic manifestation.
Velvety patches describe Acanthosis nigricans, which is a cutaneous paraneoplastic syndrome.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) may be encountered in association with deep-seated cancers, most often carcinomas of the pancreas or lung.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
coreConcept: Diagnostic Contrast in Hypercalcemia of Malignancy
statement: Regarding paraneoplastic hypercalcemia in a patient with breast carcinoma, which statement best reflects the complexity of the diagnosis?
options: Hypercalcemia in breast cancer is usually due to ectopic calcitonin release.
The presence of hypercalcemia always rules out bone metastases.
Only squamous cell carcinomas produce paraneoplastic hypercalcemia.
Hypercalcemia is often exacerbated by osteolytic bone metastases in this specific cancer.
The hypercalcemia is exclusively caused by the release of PTHRP.
correctOption: Hypercalcemia is often exacerbated by osteolytic bone metastases in this specific cancer.
optionExplanations: Calcitonin release would actually lower serum calcium; paraneoplastic hypercalcemia involves factors that increase serum calcium like PTHRP, IL-1, or TGF-alpha.
Hypercalcemia does not rule out bone metastases; in fact, the two often coexist and worsen the hypercalcemic state.
While squamous cell carcinomas are frequently associated with paraneoplastic hypercalcemia, it also occurs in carcinomas of the breast, kidney, and ovary.
In breast carcinoma, the humoral paraneoplastic mechanism (PTHRP or other factors) and the direct anatomical effect of osteolytic bone metastases often combine to produce hypercalcemia.
Hypercalcemia in breast cancer is often multifactorial, involving both humoral mechanisms (like PTHRP) and direct bone destruction.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): In breast cancers, paraneoplastic hypercalcemia is often exacerbated by osteolytic bone metastases.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 72-year-old female with advanced mucin-secreting gastric adenocarcinoma suddenly develops right-sided weakness and a facial droop. An echocardiogram reveals small, bland, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations on the mitral valve. What is the most likely diagnosis for the cardiac finding, and what is its clinical risk?
options: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis; risk of systemic emboli
Infective endocarditis; risk of valvular perforation
Rheumatic heart disease; risk of mitral stenosis
Libman-Sacks endocarditis; risk of cardiac tamponade
Trousseau syndrome; risk of deep vein thrombosis
correctOption: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis; risk of systemic emboli
optionExplanations: NBTE involves sterile vegetations on heart valves in advanced cancer patients (especially mucin-secreting ones). These are highly friable and carry a high risk of embolizing to the brain, causing stroke.
Infective endocarditis involves microbial infection and typically produces large, friable vegetations and fever, which are not present here.
Rheumatic heart disease is a sequela of streptococcal infection and usually results in valvular scarring and fusion over years, not acute bland vegetations in a cancer patient.
Libman-Sacks endocarditis occurs in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), and while the vegetations are sterile, it is not the primary association for mucin-secreting gastric cancer.
Trousseau syndrome refers to migratory clots in the peripheral veins, not vegetations on the heart valves.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Bland, small, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations... called nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis... are potential sources of emboli that can further complicate the course of the cancer.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
coreConcept: Metabolic Mechanism of Paraneoplastic Cushing Syndrome
statement: A patient with a lung mass presents with truncal obesity, 'moon facies,' and purple abdominal striae. Laboratory testing confirms ectopic production of a hormone-like substance. Which of the following describes the most likely physiological loop occurring in this paraneoplastic syndrome?
options: Tumor production of ACTH-like peptides stimulating the adrenal cortex to release cortisol.
Tumor production of PTHRP increasing renal calcium reabsorption.
Tumor production of Erythropoietin stimulating the bone marrow to produce red cells.
Tumor production of ADH-like peptides leading to excessive water retention.
Tumor production of insulin-like factors causing systemic hypoglycemia.
correctOption: Tumor production of ACTH-like peptides stimulating the adrenal cortex to release cortisol.
optionExplanations: In paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome (common in small cell lung cancer), the tumor produces corticotropin (ACTH) or ACTH-like peptides, which stimulate the adrenal glands to overproduce cortisol, leading to the clinical features described.
PTHRP production explains hypercalcemia, not the obesity and striae associated with Cushing syndrome.
Erythropoietin production would lead to polycythemia (elevated hematocrit), not obesity or facies changes.
ADH-like peptides cause SIADH (water retention and hyponatremia), which presents with neurological symptoms due to low sodium, not Cushing syndrome.
Insulin-like factors would cause hypoglycemia, presenting with confusion or syncope, not Cushingoid features.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 272 (Book Page): For example, bronchogenic carcinomas may produce corticotropin... giving rise to paraneoplastic syndromes.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
coreConcept: Primary Tumor Associations of Acanthosis Nigricans
statement: Acanthosis nigricans, a velvety hyperpigmentation of the skin often seen in paraneoplastic syndromes, is most classically associated with which of the following primary malignancies?
options: Hepatocellular carcinoma
Carcinoma of the stomach
Acute promyelocytic leukemia
Bronchogenic carcinoma
Renal cell adenocarcinoma
correctOption: Carcinoma of the stomach
optionExplanations: Hepatocellular carcinoma typically causes syndromes like polycythemia or hypoglycemia rather than specific hyperkeratotic skin changes.
Gastric carcinoma is the most classic and frequently cited malignancy associated with the paraneoplastic presentation of Acanthosis nigricans in adults.
Acute promyelocytic leukemia is classically associated with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), not Acanthosis nigricans.
While lung cancer has many paraneoplastic syndromes, it is not the most common primary tumor associated with Acanthosis nigricans.
Renal cell carcinoma is more commonly associated with paraneoplastic hypercalcemia or polycythemia than with Acanthosis nigricans.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): In about 50% of the cases... the appearance of such lesions is associated with cancer, most commonly carcinoma of the stomach.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which of the following best defines a paraneoplastic syndrome in the context of clinical oncology?
options: Clinical symptoms caused by the direct compression of surrounding tissues by the primary tumor mass.
The systemic effects of cachexia, including weight loss and muscle wasting, caused by tumor-induced cytokine release.
Symptom complexes that cannot be explained by the local or distant spread of the tumor or by the release of hormones indigenous to the tissue of origin.
Metastatic deposits in the endocrine glands that lead to the overproduction of specific regulatory hormones.
The direct invasion of the central nervous system by malignant cells resulting in focal neurological deficits.
correctOption: Symptom complexes that cannot be explained by the local or distant spread of the tumor or by the release of hormones indigenous to the tissue of origin.
optionExplanations: Symptoms caused by direct compression or local invasion are primary clinical effects of the tumor mass, not paraneoplastic syndromes.

Cachexia is a common systemic effect of cancer involving cytokine release (like TNF), but it is generally categorized separately from the specific symptom complexes defined as paraneoplastic syndromes in clinical diagnosis.

Paraneoplastic syndromes are specifically defined as signs and symptoms occurring at sites distant from the tumor or its metastases that are not explained by the normal physiological functions of the original cell type.
Hormone overproduction from metastatic invasion of an endocrine gland is a direct effect of metastasis, whereas paraneoplastic syndromes often involve 'ectopic' hormone production.
Direct invasion of the CNS is a local or metastatic effect; paraneoplastic neurological syndromes are typically immune-mediated rather than due to physical tumor presence.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Paraneoplastic syndromes: symptom complexes in individuals with cancer that cannot be explained by tumor spread or release of hormones that are indigenous to the tumor “cell of origin.”

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A patient with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung develops significant hypercalcemia. Which mechanism is most likely responsible for this paraneoplastic manifestation?
options: Production and release of parathyroid hormone–related protein (PTHRP) by the tumor.
Secondary hyperparathyroidism resulting from chronic renal failure induced by tumor lysis syndrome.
Tumor-induced activation of Vitamin D through the ectopic expression of 1-alpha-hydroxylase.
Excessive secretion of calcitonin by the malignant epithelial cells.
Direct osteolytic destruction of bone by metastatic tumor cells.
correctOption: Production and release of parathyroid hormone–related protein (PTHRP) by the tumor.
optionExplanations: PTHRP is a common ectopic factor produced by squamous cell carcinomas that mimics the action of PTH, leading to bone resorption and hypercalcemia without necessitating bone metastases.

Secondary hyperparathyroidism usually results in low or normal calcium levels with high phosphate; it is not the primary paraneoplastic mechanism for lung-cancer-induced hypercalcemia mentioned in the text.
While some lymphomas can produce dihydroxyvitamin D, PTHRP is the specific factor linked to squamous cell carcinomas of the lung in the reference text.
Calcitonin acts to lower serum calcium levels; its elevation (as seen in medullary thyroid carcinoma) would not cause hypercalcemia.

While osteolytic metastases can cause hypercalcemia, the question specifically asks for the mechanism in the context of a paraneoplastic syndrome, where PTHRP is the most common mediator for squamous cell carcinomas.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The most common lung neoplasm associated with hypercalcemia is squamous cell carcinoma, typically because of release of PTHRP.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: In the clinical evaluation of paraneoplastic skin disorders, how does Acanthosis nigricans typically differ from the Leser-Trélat sign?
options: Acanthosis nigricans involves gray-black hyperkeratotic patches, whereas Leser-Trélat involves the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses.
Acanthosis nigricans is caused by hormone release, while the Leser-Trélat sign is caused by direct skin invasion.
Acanthosis nigricans is always benign, while the Leser-Trélat sign is only found in malignant cases.
Acanthosis nigricans is associated only with lung cancer, while Leser-Trélat is specific to prostatic adenocarcinoma.
The Leser-Trélat sign occurs exclusively in juveniles, while Acanthosis nigricans occurs only in adults over age 40.
correctOption: Acanthosis nigricans involves gray-black hyperkeratotic patches, whereas Leser-Trélat involves the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses.
optionExplanations: Acanthosis nigricans presents as velvety, hyperpigmented plaques, while the Leser-Trélat sign is the sudden eruption of numerous seborrheic keratoses, both of which can be markers of internal malignancy.
Neither condition is caused by direct skin invasion; they are paraneoplastic and thought to be mediated by growth factors produced by the tumor, such as TGF-alpha or EGF.
The text states Acanthosis nigricans occurs rarely as a genetically determined disease (benign), and in 50% of cases is associated with cancer; thus, it is not 'always' benign.
The text associates Acanthosis nigricans most commonly with carcinoma of the stomach, not lung cancer.
Acanthosis nigricans can occur in juveniles as a genetic disease or in adults in association with malignancy.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Acanthosis nigricans is a disorder characterized by gray-black patches of thickened, hyperkeratotic skin with a velvety appearance... Acanthosis nigricans is sometimes accompanied by the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses (Leser-Trélat sign).

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 64-year-old male presents with epigastric pain, weight loss, and obstructive jaundice. Physical examination reveals tender, erythematous, linear cords along the superficial veins of his left arm and right thigh that seem to resolve and reappear in different locations. What is the most likely paraneoplastic mechanism underlying these vascular findings?
options: Migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) associated with a deep-seated visceral malignancy.
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis resulting in systemic arterial embolization.
Direct invasion of the major venous walls by metastatic adenocarcinoma cells.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) secondary to acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Bacterial infection of the superficial venous valves due to immunosuppression.
correctOption: Migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) associated with a deep-seated visceral malignancy.
optionExplanations: The presentation of migratory thrombophlebitis in a patient with symptoms of pancreatic cancer (jaundice, weight loss) is classic for Trousseau syndrome.
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) involves heart valve vegetations and emboli, but it does not typically present as tender, migratory venous cords on the limbs.
Migratory thrombophlebitis occurs at sites distant from the primary tumor and is mediated by tumor-released procoagulants, not by direct malignant invasion of every affected vein.
While DIC can occur in cancer, it usually presents with generalized bleeding or microthrombi rather than localized, migratory superficial thrombophlebitis.
The 'migratory' nature and association with cancer symptoms make a primary infectious etiology less likely than a paraneoplastic procoagulant state.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) may be encountered in association with deep-seated cancers, most often carcinomas of the pancreas or lung.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Certain bronchogenic carcinomas produce Cushing syndrome. Which biochemical step in the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis is bypassed in these cases?
options: The physiological suppression of ACTH by the anterior pituitary gland.
The conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone within the mitochondria.
The synthesis of cortisol by the adrenal cortex.
The requirement for pituitary-derived ACTH due to ectopic production by the tumor.
The negative feedback loop of cortisol on the malignant lung cells.
correctOption: The requirement for pituitary-derived ACTH due to ectopic production by the tumor.
optionExplanations: Pituitary ACTH is suppressed by high cortisol levels, but the tumor-derived ACTH is not subject to this pituitary regulation.
The biochemical pathway of steroidogenesis in the adrenal gland remains intact but is hyperactive due to excessive ACTH stimulation.
Adrenal cortisol synthesis still occurs; it is actually overstimulated by the ectopic ACTH produced by the tumor.
In paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome, the tumor produces corticotropin (ACTH) autonomously, bypassing the normal pituitary source and its regulatory controls.
Malignant lung cells generally do not possess the receptors or feedback mechanisms of the normal anterior pituitary, thus they continue to produce ACTH regardless of cortisol levels.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 272 (Book Page): For example, bronchogenic carcinomas may produce corticotropin, parathyroid-like hormone, insulin, glucagon, and other hormones, giving rise to paraneoplastic syndromes.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Which set of clinical features most accurately describes Hypertrophic Osteoarthropathy when it occurs as a paraneoplastic syndrome?
options: Symmetrical polyarthritis of the small joints of the hands and morning stiffness.
Periosteal new bone formation, arthritis of adjacent joints, and clubbing of the digits.
Erosion of the distal phalanges and hypercalcemia due to PTHRP.
Generalized osteoporosis and increased risk of pathologic fractures in long bones.
Bland vegetations on the cardiac valves and peripheral splinter hemorrhages.
correctOption: Periosteal new bone formation, arthritis of adjacent joints, and clubbing of the digits.
optionExplanations: This describes Rheumatoid Arthritis, whereas paraneoplastic hypertrophic osteoarthropathy involves periosteal bone and clubbing.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is defined by the triad of periosteal proliferation, joint inflammation, and finger clubbing, often associated with lung cancer.
Hypercalcemia and osteoarthropathy are both paraneoplastic, but they are distinct syndromes; osteoarthropathy involves bone formation, not erosion.
Osteoporosis is a loss of bone density; hypertrophic osteoarthropathy involves the pathological addition of new bone under the periosteum.
These features are characteristic of endocarditis (infectious or NBTE), not skeletal/joint paraneoplastic syndromes.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): This disorder is characterized by (1) periosteal new bone formation, primarily at the distal ends of long bones... (2) arthritis of the adjacent joints; and (3) clubbing of the digits.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: Patients with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas are at specific risk for developing which paraneoplastic cardiovascular complication?
options: Myocardial infarction secondary to direct tumor emboli in the coronary arteries.
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) involving fibrinous vegetations on cardiac valves.
High-output heart failure due to tumor-induced arteriovenous shunting.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy driven by ectopic growth hormone production.
Acute pericarditis caused by the systemic release of inflammatory interleukins.
correctOption: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) involving fibrinous vegetations on cardiac valves.
optionExplanations: Myocardial infarction in these patients is more likely due to NBTE-related emboli than 'direct' tumor cells in the coronary arteries.
Mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas (like those of the pancreas or lung) can trigger the formation of sterile, bland vegetations on valves, which are a major source of emboli.
Arteriovenous shunting is a localized effect of some large tumors, but it is not the specific paraneoplastic complication associated with mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas in the text.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is not a recognized paraneoplastic syndrome associated with mucin production; growth hormone excess would cause acromegaly.
While inflammation is common in cancer, specific fibrinous valve vegetations are the hallmark paraneoplastic heart finding mentioned.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Bland, small, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations sometimes form on the cardiac valve leaflets... particularly in individuals with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas. These lesions, called nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis...

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: A 70-year-old heavy smoker is found to have a central lung mass on imaging. He reports progressive weakness in his proximal leg muscles that improves significantly after brief physical exercise. Which pathophysiological mechanism best explains this paraneoplastic syndrome?
options: Severe hypokalemia resulting from the ectopic production of aldosterone by the tumor cells.
Direct compression of the lumbosacral plexus by a rapidly expanding primary tumor.
Widespread skeletal muscle necrosis caused by tumor-derived Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF).
Destruction of the acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction by autoantibodies.
An immunologic attack on normal tissues induced by the ectopic expression of neuronal antigens by the tumor.
correctOption: An immunologic attack on normal tissues induced by the ectopic expression of neuronal antigens by the tumor.
optionExplanations: Ectopic aldosterone is not listed in the common paraneoplastic syndromes; Cushing's (ACTH) is the common lung-related endocrinopathy.
Weakness that improves with exercise (Lambert-Eaton) is a functional paraneoplastic phenomenon, whereas nerve compression results in persistent or worsening deficits.
TNF-alpha mediates cachexia (muscle wasting), but specific myasthenic-like weakness is an immune-mediated neuromyopathic syndrome.

Acetylcholine receptor destruction is the mechanism of Myasthenia Gravis; the paraneoplastic 'myasthenic syndrome' (Lambert-Eaton) typically involves presynaptic calcium channels, though both represent immunologic attacks on the neuromuscular system.
Neuromyopathic syndromes (like the myasthenic syndrome mentioned in the text) are thought to be immune-mediated, triggered by tumor antigens that mimic neural or muscle proteins.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The cause of these syndromes is poorly understood, but appears to involve a cancer-induced immunologic attack on normal tissues. The initiating event may be the ectopic expression of antigens that normally are restricted to the neuromuscular system by tumor cells.

category: Describe the clinical features of common paraneoplastic syndromes
statement: The development of a paraneoplastic neuromyopathic syndrome, such as cortical cerebellar degeneration, is primarily attributed to which physiological loop?
options: A hypermetabolic state that depletes essential neurotrophic factors from the cerebellum.
Chronic hypoxia of the brain tissue caused by paraneoplastic erythrocytosis and hyperviscosity.
The production of cross-reactive antibodies or T-cell responses against neuronal antigens expressed by the tumor.
Increased intracranial pressure due to the secretion of excessive cerebrospinal fluid by the tumor.
The accumulation of neurotoxic metabolic by-products like ammonia due to tumor-induced liver failure.
correctOption: The production of cross-reactive antibodies or T-cell responses against neuronal antigens expressed by the tumor.
optionExplanations: Depletion of neurotrophic factors is not the described mechanism for these paraneoplastic syndromes.
Hyperviscosity can cause neurological symptoms, but paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration is specifically characterized as an 'immunologic attack'.
