coreConcept: Multifaceted Paraneoplastic Presentation of Lung Carcinoma
statement: A 68-year-old male with a 50-pack-year smoking history presents with a persistent cough, hemoptysis, and recent onset of swelling and tenderness in his wrists and ankles. Physical examination reveals digital clubbing and periosteal new bone formation on X-ray of the distal radius. Laboratory evaluation reveals hypercalcemia. Which underlying neoplastic diagnosis and paraneoplastic combination is most probable?
options: Small cell lung carcinoma with Cushing syndrome and SIADH
Gastric adenocarcinoma with acanthosis nigricans and Leser-Trélat sign
Acute promyelocytic leukemia with disseminated intravascular coagulation
Squamous cell lung carcinoma with hypertrophic osteoarthropathy and PTHRP-mediated hypercalcemia
Pancreatic adenocarcinoma with Trousseau syndrome and hypoglycemia
correctOption: Squamous cell lung carcinoma with hypertrophic osteoarthropathy and PTHRP-mediated hypercalcemia
optionExplanations: Small cell lung cancer is associated with ACTH (Cushing) and SIADH, but the musculoskeletal symptoms (clubbing/periosteal bone) and hypercalcemia point strongly to squamous cell carcinoma.
Gastric cancer is linked to skin signs, but does not typically cause clubbing or PTHRP-mediated hypercalcemia.
While DIC is a paraneoplastic-like complication of leukemia, it presents with bleeding/clotting issues, not skeletal remodeling or ectopic hormone symptoms like clubbing and hypercalcemia.

The clinical picture of digital clubbing and periosteal bone formation (hypertrophic osteoarthropathy) combined with hypercalcemia is a classic paraneoplastic constellation for lung carcinoma, specifically the squamous cell subtype.
Pancreatic cancer is associated with migratory thrombophlebitis, not the specific periosteal bone changes or hypercalcemia described.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is encountered in 1% to 10% of patients with lung carcinoma. ...characterized by (1) periosteal new bone formation... (2) arthritis... and (3) clubbing... The most common lung neoplasm associated with hypercalcemia is squamous cell carcinoma, typically because of release of PTHRP.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: Migratory thrombophlebitis, characterized by successive crops of tender venous nodules, is most classically associated with which of the following deep-seated malignancies?
options: Bronchogenic carcinoma
Renal tubular adenoma
Prostatic adenocarcinoma
Pancreatic carcinoma
Hepatocellular carcinoma
correctOption: Pancreatic carcinoma
optionExplanations: While lung cancer can be associated with Trousseau syndrome, pancreatic carcinoma is the most classic and frequently cited association in clinical pathology.
Renal tubular adenoma is a benign tumor and does not typically present with paraneoplastic syndromes like migratory thrombophlebitis.
Prostatic adenocarcinoma is more commonly associated with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), not migratory thrombophlebitis.
Trousseau syndrome (migratory thrombophlebitis) is a classic paraneoplastic manifestation of visceral malignancies, most notably those of the pancreas.
Hepatocellular carcinoma typically presents with other paraneoplastic signs like erythrocytosis or hypoglycemia rather than Trousseau syndrome.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) may be encountered in association with deep-seated cancers, most often carcinomas of the pancreas or lung.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
coreConcept: Ectopic Hormone Production in Bronchogenic Carcinoma
statement: Which of the following hormones is most frequently produced ectopically by a bronchogenic carcinoma, leading to the development of paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome?
options: Thyroglobulin
Glucagon
Parathyroid-like hormone
Insulin
Corticotropin
correctOption: Corticotropin
optionExplanations: Thyroglobulin is a marker for thyroid tissue and is not associated with paraneoplastic Cushing syndrome.
Ectopic glucagon would affect glucose levels, whereas Cushing syndrome specifically requires excess glucocorticoids driven by ACTH/Corticotropin.
Parathyroid-like hormone (PTHRP) causes hypercalcemia, not Cushing syndrome.
Ectopic insulin production causes hypoglycemia, not Cushing syndrome.
Cushing syndrome in the context of lung cancer is usually driven by the ectopic secretion of ACTH (corticotropin) by the neoplastic cells.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 272 (Book Page): For example, bronchogenic carcinomas may produce corticotropin, parathyroid-like hormone, insulin, glucagon, and other hormones, giving rise to paraneoplastic syndromes.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: The development of Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) as a paraneoplastic manifestation is most frequently documented in which pair of neoplasms?
options: Breast adenocarcinoma and Osteosarcoma
Gastric carcinoma and Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Hepatocellular carcinoma and Renal cell carcinoma
Acute promyelocytic leukemia and Prostatic adenocarcinoma
Small cell lung cancer and Follicular lymphoma
correctOption: Acute promyelocytic leukemia and Prostatic adenocarcinoma
optionExplanations: Breast cancer and osteosarcoma are not the most common associations for paraneoplastic DIC.
While pancreatic cancer is associated with Trousseau syndrome, DIC is more classically linked to the prostate and APL in the paraneoplastic context.
These tumors have other paraneoplastic associations, but DIC is not their primary paraneoplastic hallmark.
Both acute promyelocytic leukemia (due to procoagulant release from granules) and prostatic adenocarcinoma are major neoplastic causes of DIC.
Small cell lung cancer has endocrine paraneoplastic syndromes, and lymphomas are not the typical drivers for acute paraneoplastic DIC.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Disseminated intravascular coagulation may complicate a diversity of clinical disorders... among cancers, it is most commonly associated with acute promyelocytic leukemia and prostatic adenocarcinoma.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: A 61-year-old female with advanced, mucin-secreting colonic adenocarcinoma is found to have small, bland, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations on her mitral valve during an echocardiographic work-up for a suspected embolic stroke. What is the most likely diagnosis for this cardiac complication?
options: Rheumatic heart disease
Libman-Sacks endocarditis
Infective endocarditis
Atrial myxoma
Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
correctOption: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
optionExplanations: Rheumatic heart disease is an immunologic sequel to Group A Streptococcal infection, not a paraneoplastic syndrome.
Libman-Sacks endocarditis is associated with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), not typically as a paraneoplastic sign of adenocarcinoma.
Infective endocarditis involves microbial colonization of valves, whereas paraneoplastic vegetations are specifically 'bland' and 'nonbacterial'.
An atrial myxoma is a primary heart tumor, not a paraneoplastic valvular vegetation resulting from an external adenocarcinoma.

Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) is a recognized paraneoplastic syndrome where sterile vegetations form on valves, classically seen in patients with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Bland, small, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations sometimes form on the cardiac valve leaflets... particularly in individuals with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas. These lesions, called nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis...

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
coreConcept: Correlation of Acanthosis Nigricans with Gastric Neoplasms
statement: A 52-year-old male presents with gray-black, velvety, hyperkeratotic patches in his axillae and neck. Clinical evaluation reveals a lesion in the stomach. Which of the following is the most likely paraneoplastic correlation for this cutaneous manifestation?
options: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Gastric carcinoma
Small cell carcinoma of the lung
Renal cell carcinoma
Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung
correctOption: Gastric carcinoma
optionExplanations: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is most commonly associated with migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome), not the specific dermatologic changes described here.
Acanthosis nigricans in adults over 40 is a classic paraneoplastic marker strongly associated with abdominal malignancies, with gastric carcinoma being the most frequent culprit.

Small cell carcinoma of the lung is more classically associated with ectopic ACTH production (Cushing syndrome) or ADH secretion (SIADH), rather than the specific velvety skin patches of acanthosis nigricans.
Renal cell carcinoma is associated with paraneoplastic erythropoietin production leading to polycythemia or hypercalcemia, but not typically acanthosis nigricans.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung is the most common cause of humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy via PTHRP, not acanthosis nigricans.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Acanthosis nigricans is a disorder characterized by gray-black patches of thickened, hyperkeratotic skin with a velvety appearance. ... In about 50% of the cases, particularly in adults older than age 40, the appearance of such lesions is associated with cancer, most commonly carcinoma of the stomach.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
coreConcept: Mechanism of Humoral Hypercalcemia of Malignancy (HHM)
statement: In the context of humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung, which pathophysiological mechanism is primarily responsible for the elevation of serum calcium levels in the absence of bony metastases?
options: Direct osteolysis by tumor cell infiltration
Production of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHRP)
Ectopic secretion of native parathyroid hormone (PTH)
Secretory release of Vitamin D precursors
Inhibition of calcitonin secretion by C-cells
correctOption: Production of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHRP)
optionExplanations: Direct osteolysis refers to bone destruction by metastatic deposits; however, paraneoplastic hypercalcemia occurs humrally even without such physical spread.
PTHRP is a protein produced by various tumors (especially lung SCC) that mimics the action of PTH on bone and kidney, leading to hypercalcemia without needing direct bone destruction.
Native PTH is rarely secreted ectopically by tumors; the paraneoplastic syndrome is usually caused by a related but distinct protein (PTHRP) that shares N-terminal homology.
While some lymphomas can produce 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, this is not the primary mechanism in squamous cell carcinomas of the lung.
Hypercalcemia in malignancy is driven by bone resorption and renal calcium retention, not by a primary deficiency or inhibition of calcitonin, which is a relatively weak regulator in this context.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The most common lung neoplasm associated with hypercalcemia is squamous cell carcinoma, typically because of release of PTHRP.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: Which of the following clinical features distinguishes Trousseau syndrome from nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) in a patient with a deep-seated malignancy?
options: Primary involvement of the left-sided cardiac valves
Development of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
Manifestation as migratory thrombophlebitis
Association with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas
Presence of small, bland fibrinous vegetations on heart valves
correctOption: Manifestation as migratory thrombophlebitis
optionExplanations: Left-sided cardiac valve involvement is a specific characteristic of NBTE, not Trousseau syndrome, which affects veins rather than the heart valves directly.
While both can be associated with hypercoagulable states, DIC is a separate hematologic complication most common in acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Trousseau syndrome is specifically characterized by migratory thrombophlebitis (recurrent venous clots in different locations), distinguishing it from the endocardial vegetations of NBTE.
Both Trousseau syndrome and NBTE can be associated with advanced mucin-secreting adenocarcinomas, so this does not distinguish between them.
Small, bland fibrinous vegetations on heart valves are the hallmark of NBTE, whereas Trousseau syndrome involves the peripheral venous system.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) may be encountered in association with deep-seated cancers, most often carcinomas of the pancreas or lung.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
coreConcept: Ectopic ACTH Production in Small Cell Lung Cancer
statement: A 64-year-old female smoker presents with a 4-week history of worsening proximal muscle weakness, weight loss, and new-onset hypertension. On physical examination, she has 'moon' facies and purple abdominal striae. A chest X-ray reveals a central hilar mass. Laboratory tests show significant hypokalemia and elevated plasma cortisol levels that are not suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone. Which paraneoplastic syndrome and neoplastic correlation is most likely?
options: Lambert-Eaton syndrome due to Squamous cell lung carcinoma
Cushing syndrome due to Small cell lung carcinoma
Polycythemia due to Renal cell carcinoma
SIADH due to Small cell lung carcinoma
Hypercalcemia due to Squamous cell lung carcinoma
correctOption: Cushing syndrome due to Small cell lung carcinoma
optionExplanations: Lambert-Eaton is a neuromuscular paraneoplastic syndrome associated with Small cell (not Squamous cell) carcinoma, involving presynaptic calcium channel antibodies rather than endocrine changes.

Small cell lung carcinoma frequently produces ectopic ACTH (corticotropin), leading to Cushing syndrome. This is consistent with the patient's smoking history, central hilar mass, and cortisol-driven symptoms.
Polycythemia and Renal cell carcinoma do not explain the central lung mass or the classic Cushingoid appearance of the patient.
SIADH causes hyponatremia and fluid retention, which does not match the 'moon' facies and hypertension seen in this Cushingoid presentation.
The patient's symptoms (moon facies, striae, hypertension) are indicative of hypercortisolism (Cushing), not hypercalcemia, which typically presents with stones, moans, and groans.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 272 (Book Page): For example, bronchogenic carcinomas may produce corticotropin, parathyroid-like hormone, insulin, glucagon, and other hormones, giving rise to paraneoplastic syndromes.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: In patients with advanced malignancies, nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE) represents a significant clinical risk primarily due to which of the following complications?
options: Myocardial infarction due to direct tumor invasion of the coronary arteries
Progressive valvular stenosis from organization of the thrombus
Systemic embolization of fibrinous vegetations
Secondary bacterial infection of the valve resulting in septicemia
Rupture of the chordae tendineae leading to acute heart failure
correctOption: Systemic embolization of fibrinous vegetations
optionExplanations: NBTE is a paraneoplastic, humoral effect on the endocardium, not a result of direct tumor infiltration of the coronary vasculature or myocardium.
Organization of thrombi into valvular stenosis is a slow process seen in rheumatic heart disease, whereas NBTE occurs in the terminal stages of cancer with embolic risks predominating.
The vegetations in NBTE are loosely attached and friable, making systemic embolization to the brain, kidneys, or spleen a critical and frequent complication.
While vegetations can occasionally seed, NBTE is defined as 'bland' and 'nonbacterial'; the immediate and most common threat is mechanical embolization rather than sepsis.
Chordal rupture is a characteristic of acute infective endocarditis or rheumatic disease, but it is not the typical clinical progression of NBTE.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Bland, small, nonbacterial fibrinous vegetations sometimes form on the cardiac valve leaflets... The vegetations are potential sources of emboli that can further complicate the course of the cancer.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy is a paraneoplastic syndrome that includes a triad of clinical findings. Which of the following is specifically included in this triad and is most frequently associated with lung carcinoma?
options: Migratory thrombophlebitis, endocarditis, and hypercalcemia
Encephalitis, cerebellar degeneration, and neuropathy
Clubbing of the digits, periosteal new bone formation, and arthritis
Acanthosis nigricans, arthritis, and skin thickening
Venous thrombosis, arterial embolism, and heart murmurs
correctOption: Clubbing of the digits, periosteal new bone formation, and arthritis
optionExplanations: This option lists various vascular and endocrine syndromes that are not related to the skeletal triad of osteoarthropathy.
Encephalitis and cerebellar degeneration belong to the neuromyopathic paraneoplastic syndromes, which are distinct from the skeletal findings.
The classic triad of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy consists of digit clubbing, periosteal reaction/new bone formation (often visible on X-ray), and symmetric arthritis.
Acanthosis nigricans is a separate skin-related paraneoplastic syndrome, not part of the skeletal/joint findings of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.
Venous thrombosis and arterial embolism are complications of Trousseau syndrome and NBTE, not features of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy itself.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): This disorder is characterized by (1) periosteal new bone formation, primarily at the distal ends of long bones... (2) arthritis of the adjacent joints; and (3) clubbing of the digits.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: A 58-year-old male with a history of heavy smoking and a persistent cough is found to have a serum calcium level of 13.5 mg/dL. He has no evidence of bone metastasis on a radionuclide bone scan. If this is a paraneoplastic syndrome, which set of factors secreted by the tumor is likely mediating this metabolic derangement besides PTHRP?
options: ACTH and insulin-like growth factors
Serotonin and histamine
Gastrin and glucagon
IL-1, TGF-α, and TNF
Erythropoietin and renin
correctOption: IL-1, TGF-α, and TNF
optionExplanations: ACTH leads to Cushing syndrome, not hypercalcemia. Insulin-like growth factors are more likely related to hypoglycemia syndromes in large mesenchymal tumors.
Serotonin and histamine are associated with the carcinoid syndrome, which presents with flushing and diarrhea rather than hypercalcemia.
Gastrin causes Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (peptic ulcers) and glucagon causes necrolytic migratory erythema; neither are implicated in hypercalcemia of malignancy.
Paraneoplastic hypercalcemia is multi-factorial; while PTHRP is the most common cause, cytokines like IL-1, TNF, and TGF-alpha also stimulate osteoclast activity and increase serum calcium.
Erythropoietin causes polycythemia, and renin would cause hypertension; neither are primary drivers of paraneoplastic hypercalcemia.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): In addition to PTHRP, several other factors, such as IL-1, TGF-α, TNF, and dihydroxyvitamin D, have been causally implicated in the hypercalcemia of malignancy.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
coreConcept: The Leser-Trélat Sign and Gastric Adenocarcinoma
statement: A 45-year-old female presents with the sudden appearance of numerous itchy seborrheic keratoses on her trunk (Leser-Trélat sign). Further diagnostic workup reveals an underlying malignancy. Based on paraneoplastic correlations, which primary site of neoplasia is most statistically probable?
options: Stomach
Brain (Glial cells)
Thyroid gland
Urinary bladder
Bone marrow
correctOption: Stomach
optionExplanations: The Leser-Trélat sign is an eruptive form of seborrheic keratoses often occurring alongside acanthosis nigricans as a paraneoplastic indicator of internal malignancy, specifically gastric adenocarcinoma.
Brain tumors (gliomas) rarely metastasize or produce systemic cutaneous paraneoplastic signs like the Leser-Trélat sign.
Thyroid cancers are more likely to present with local symptoms or medullary-specific markers like calcitonin, not the sudden eruptive seborrheic keratoses of Leser-Trélat.
Bladder cancer is not a classic association for the Leser-Trélat sign, which is most strongly linked to GI tract adenocarcinomas.
Bone marrow malignancies (leukemias/lymphomas) may cause skin infiltration or different paraneoplastic effects, but Leser-Trélat is a hallmark of solid abdominal viscera cancers, primarily stomach.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): Acanthosis nigricans is sometimes accompanied by the abrupt development of multiple seborrheic keratoses (Leser-Trélat sign). ... associated with cancer, most commonly carcinoma of the stomach.

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: In the physiological regulation of red blood cell mass, certain tumors can cause polycythemia by creating a pathological metabolic loop. Which neoplastic lesion is correctly correlated with the paraneoplastic production of erythropoietin?
options: Gastric adenocarcinoma
Small cell carcinoma of the lung
Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung
Renal cell carcinoma
correctOption: Renal cell carcinoma
optionExplanations: Gastric adenocarcinoma is most famously linked to acanthosis nigricans and the Leser-Trélat sign, not polycythemia.
Small cell carcinoma of the lung is the 'great imitator' for Cushing's (ACTH) and SIADH (ADH), but is not a primary cause of paraneoplastic polycythemia.
Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is mostly associated with hypercoagulable states (Trousseau) and NBTE, not erythropoietin secretion.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung is primarily linked to hypercalcemia (PTHRP), not erythropoietin production.
Renal cell carcinoma is a classic producer of ectopic erythropoietin, which stimulates the bone marrow to produce excessive red blood cells, leading to polycythemia.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page) Table 7.11: Polycythemia ... Erythropoietin ... Renal carcinoma, cerebellar hemangioma, hepatocellular carcinoma

category: Correlate specific paraneoplastic syndromes with their corresponding neoplastic lesions
statement: Which of the following paraneoplastic syndromes is characterized by an immunologic attack on normal tissues, specifically suspected to involve cross-reactive antibodies against neuronal cell antigens?
options: Neuromyopathic syndromes
Acanthosis nigricans
Migratory thrombophlebitis
Cushing syndrome
Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy
correctOption: Neuromyopathic syndromes
optionExplanations: Neuromyopathic syndromes (like cerebellar degeneration or myasthenic syndromes) are thought to occur when the immune system attacks neurons due to cross-reactivity with tumor antigens.
Acanthosis nigricans is likely driven by growth factors (like TGF-alpha) acting on skin receptors, rather than a neuronal autoimmune attack.
Migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) is a vascular phenomenon related to procoagulant release from the tumor, not an autoimmune response against neurons.
Cushing syndrome is an endocrine paraneoplastic effect caused by ectopic hormone production (ACTH), not an autoimmune attack.
Hypercalcemia is caused by humoral factors (like PTHRP) that affect bone and kidney physiology, not an antibody-mediated attack.
citation: In book "Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease", Page 330 (Book Page): The neuromyopathic paraneoplastic syndromes ... appears to involve a cancer-induced immunologic attack on normal tissues. ... in some cases, antibodies that cross-react with neuronal cell antigens are detected.
